title: X - the same judgment asked as Noul, Score and Choice
note: One underlying quantity, three primitives, one request. The docs argue a Noul value is not a scale of the thing asked about: it is the probability that a proposition is true. The Score, whose levels the caller defines, is what actually measures degree. This case puts both next to a Choice so the difference is visible in numbers rather than prose.

strong_in_python.instructions: Is the candidate strong in Python?

used_python_at_work.instructions: Does the resume state that the candidate has used Python at work?
used_python_at_work.note_for_readers: The docs' example of a well-bounded yes/no, next to the vague one above.

python_experience.instructions: How much Python experience does the candidate have?
criteria: Some familiarity, such as small scripts or coursework

python_bucket.instructions: Which bucket best describes the candidate's Python experience?

criteria.familiar: Some familiarity, such as small scripts or coursework

states.state: My experience is in Java and Go. I have not used Python.
I have used Python occasionally for small scripts alongside my main Java work.
I used Python every day for two years in my last job, mostly data pipelines.
I have written Python daily for eight years, including maintaining a large Django codebase.

relations.note: Printed side by side: the Noul jumps 0.14 -> 0.81 between two adjacent candidates while the Score moves one level. The Noul spacing is not a scale.
